posts.content:
One of carbon accounting's most important datasets is going fully open source — pipeline and all.

We’re proud to partner with AdAstra Sustainability to open-source the code behind Orbae, the leading land use change (LUC) dataset. It will live as part of the Cornerstone Sustainability Data Initiative, which is also home of the USEEIO, CEDA, Emissions Factor Hub, and eGRID.

Land use change is the biggest number in a lot of carbon footprints. For high-risk commodities such as cocoa, it can account for over 90% of total product emissions. It's also the least consistent. Companies, standard-setters and regulators have largely worked from varying, incompatible datasets, making it difficult to agree on where land conversion carries the highest carbon cost. 

That's a problem for decarbonization decisions — and it’s about to matter even more. Starting January 2027, companies will be required to report land use change emissions under the GHG Protocol's new Land Sector and Removals Standard.

We see an open-source approach that invites collaboration from the broader community as the fastest way to advance the underlying science. We hope it will enable companies across the industry to make and report on their land use change impacts using a shared, trusted foundation.

More on the partnership 👉 https://lnkd.in/gAYTJ68p

✅ The simplified ESRS have passed scrutiny - there is no more uncertainty on what standards EU companies in scope for CSRD need to follow

❓ What happened: Last Friday, the Simplified ESRS officially passed technical scrutiny from the European Parliament (as expected!).

⁉️ Why this matters: This was the last procedural step before the Simplified ESRS became law. The standards, though streamlined, remain the most comprehensive sustainability disclosures anywhere in the world. 

⏭️ What's next: The Simplified ESRS will be published in the Official Journal of the EU shortly. Reminder: they do not need to be transposed. Wave 1 companies have the option to follow the old or the Simplified ESRS for next year's reporting. Wave 2 companies must follow the Simplified ESRS in 2028 reporting.

Watershed has written two guides to help companies understand the simplified ESRS – one for Wave 1 companies moving from the old standards to the new, and another for companies just getting started. Link in comments.

posts.content:
In Colombia’s Western Andes, nearly 100,000 native trees are helping reconnect one of the planet’s most biodiverse and fragmented ecosystems.

This work is led by ClimeCo, one of Watershed’s decarbonization solutions partners. In Antioquia, ClimeCo is working with Saving Nature and Fundación Bioconservancy to restore a cloud forest within the Mesenia-Paramillo Nature Reserve, in a region home to over one-sixth of all known species.Through Watershed, companies can help fund projects like this one.

The project combines active reforestation with natural regeneration, using more than 400 native tree species to rebuild wildlife corridors and give species room to migrate as the climate shifts. Its scope covers 556 hectares of reforestation and the long-term protection of 3,500 hectares, with over 250,000 tonnes of CO₂ expected to be removed over 40 years.

The impact goes well beyond carbon. Twelve women-led community nurseries have supplied nearly 100,000 native seedlings, creating stable incomes that support better housing, healthcare, education, and food security for local families. Former poachers now manage camera traps that monitor the wildlife they once hunted. Together, local residents have become central to protecting and restoring the landscape for the long term. 

Watershed customers are funding this work through the purchase of carbon credits facilitated by Watershed’s decarbonization solutions team—supporting long-term forest restoration, local livelihoods, and the protection of critical wildlife habitat.

This is part of our supplier spotlight series, introducing the partners behind the climate projects available to Watershed customers.

The big news this month: on July 3, the European Commission formally adopted the simplified ESRS—the green light companies have been waiting for to move forward with CSRD reporting. Also in Europe, the Commission adopted a voluntary ESRS for companies outside CSRD's scope, and a first draft of the ESRS for Third Countries is expected by end of July.

In California, CARB extended the SB 253 scope 1 and 2 reporting deadline from August 10 to November 10, and announced a workshop on future assurance and scope 3 requirements.

All the details, and what to do next, are in the full edition. 👇

At Tufts Cove in Nova Scotia, Planetary became the first company in the world to deliver independently verified ocean alkalinity enhancement carbon-removal credits, with buyers including Shopify, Stripe, and British Airways. 

Planetary, one of Watershed’s decarbonization solutions partners, helps the ocean do more of what it already does naturally: absorb and store carbon dioxide. Its coastal ocean alkalinity enhancement approach works somewhat like an antacid—using alkaline materials to restore ocean chemistry so it can take up more CO2 and store it durably.

Working with Nova Scotia Power and Dalhousie University, Planetary has removed and delivered more than 4,850 tonnes of CO2 at Tufts Cove—roughly equivalent to the carbon sequestered by 5,000 acres of forest in one year.

Proving the science was only part of the challenge. Indigenous rights holders, fisheries representatives, regulators, researchers, and local communities have helped shape the work. When fisheries representatives raised concerns about lobster, Planetary added lobster-larvae testing to its research program. A first-of-its-kind governance committee also brings Indigenous knowledge and Western science together to guide decision-making.

Watershed customers are helping fund verified carbon removal from Planetary, along with the research, monitoring, and community participation needed to determine how this approach can scale safely and responsibly.

Across 2.5 million acres of U.S. farmland, more than 1,400 farmers are turning healthier soil into a scalable climate solution.

This work is supported by Indigo, one of Watershed’s decarbonization solutions partners. Indigo helps companies support farmers in adopting lower-impact practices like planting cover crops, reducing tillage, diversifying crop rotations, and using nitrogen fertilizer more efficiently. These changes can store more carbon in the soil while also reducing emissions from farm machinery and fertilizer use. Indigo combines digital tools, data collection software, soil data, and scientific modeling to measure the results with integrity and accuracy. 

Spanning 28 states, Indigo’s US Project No. 1  has issued over 2.1 million tons of CO₂e credits to date.

In northern Ohio, participating farmer Ronald Laubacher and his son have used cover crops like vetch and clover to reduce their reliance on commercial fertilizer—saving up to $100 per acre on parts of their farm while contributing to ongoing efforts to protect the Lake Erie watershed.

Stories like Ronald’s are playing out across the project: farmers have earned more than $17.7 million in carbon revenue to date, with at least 75% of net credit sales flowing back to growers. 

Watershed’s customers are helping fund this work by purchasing carbon credits through our decarbonization solutions team—putting more revenue in farmers’ hands and supporting regenerative practices across more acres.

Across Eastern India, spreading crushed volcanic rock on farmland is helping remove carbon while increasing tea yields by up to 20% and paddy yields by up to 35%.

Alt Carbon, one of Watershed’s decarbonization solutions partners, uses enhanced rock weathering to turn degraded agricultural land into a long-term carbon sink. By spreading finely crushed basalt across farmland, the company accelerates a natural process that captures CO₂ and stores it for more than 1,000 years. Its proprietary monitoring platform and earth-science labs track each tonne with scientific precision.

Through the Darjeeling Revival Project, Alt Carbon is working with more than 35,000 farmers across over 60,000 acres and four agro-climatic zones. The project has delivered 9,566 tonnes of verified CO₂ removal to date, marking the world's largest issuance of enhanced rock weathering credits.

The benefits extend well beyond carbon. Participating farmers have seen a rise in annual incomes,  while a majority of deployment participants in participating tea estates are women. Through community town halls (Vigyaan Krishi Sabhas), Alt Carbon has been reaching out to local stakeholders from village councils to farming communities. To date, the Darjeeling Revival Project has collected, geochemically analysed, and labelled 12,000+ soil, rock and water samples collected across Eastern India. 

Watershed customers are helping fund Alt Carbon’s scientific research, laboratory testing, and monitoring systems—supporting the growth of high-integrity carbon removal across South and Southeast Asia.

For Manthrei, reliable electricity meant replacing his diesel engine with an electric motor, increasing output, and restoring the viability of his business. Across the project, that same reliable power supports 112 small businesses, which have hired 46 additional workers.

By aggregating demand from Watershed customers, Powertrust can help finance more projects that are otherwise too small or dispersed to reach corporate buyers—bringing clean energy and economic opportunity to more communities.

Today we’re releasing a comprehensive open framework for corporate AI emissions measurement.

Companies need a defensible way to measure their AI emissions—both to meet growing demands from investors, auditors, and regulators, and to identify where they can actually reduce them. Without a consistent methodology, estimates for the same AI usage can vary by nearly 5x.

The framework covers model training, inference, data center overhead, and embodied hardware. Its three-tier approach works with whatever data a company has today, so that measurements get more precise as provider data improve.

On the reduction side, we identify practical levers companies can use today: choosing the right model for the task (energy consumption can vary 30x), selecting lower-carbon regions, and optimizing prompts.
